name: insight-functions

scripts.serve: npm run build && firebase emulators:start --only functions

//dependencies: firebase-admin and firebase-functions moved together, 2026-08-14, and had
so admin 14 was unavailable on its own and `npm ci` failed ERESOLVE on any
attempt to take it alone. 7.3.2 widens that peer range to include ^14.0.0.
The ordering is the whole story — functions first, then admin.
This CLOSED the version skew the note here used to describe: the root
tree's admin copy is ^14.2.0 and so is this one, where before they were 14
and 13. test:e2e:erasure asserts 'gone means gone' through the ROOT admin
SDK against deletions performed by THIS one, and that assertion now runs
same-version on both sides. firestore-tests/e2e-delete-account.mjs still
carries the note about 14's ESM-modular export shape (no namespace default
export, so `admin.firestore()` is not a function) — that is a property of
14 itself, not of the skew, and it stays true.
//overrides: Advisories in the Google Cloud SDK chain under firebase-admin. These are
the DEPLOYED runtime, so unlike the root tree's dev-only findings they are
worth clearing. Pinning these transitive packages takes the audit to 0.
gaxios IS NOT IN THIS LIST, and must not be added back. Overriding it to
^7.1.5 took the ENTIRE BACKEND DOWN for at least a day (2026-08-06/07):
gcp-metadata@6.1.1 asks for gaxios ^6.1.1 and reads response headers as a
plain object, res.headers['metadata-flavor']. gaxios 7 returns a fetch
Headers object, where that lookup is always undefined — so every function
threw 'Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor
header. Expected Google, got no header' and could not authenticate to any
Google API. scheduledDuelReveals failed every two hours, buildModQueue and
ledgerVelocityScan daily, and seedContentV2 on every call.
Nothing caught it: the emulator supplies its own credentials, so no test
touches the metadata path, and every gate stayed green. `npm audit` was
the only thing measuring, and it was measuring the wrong property.
Removing it costs NOTHING — the audit is still 0, because the advisory it
was added for is fixed upstream in gaxios 6.7.1, which is what
gcp-metadata now resolves. Verified, not assumed.
The general lesson for the next override here: these force a version on a
package that DECLARED a different range, so each one is a compatibility
assertion nothing tests. Prefer upgrading the dependent.
This block used to end by refusing the firebase-functions 7 / admin 14
bump, on a measurement that 9 moderate advisories would become 13 with 7
high. That bump happened on 2026-08-14 (#18 then #20) and the refusal did
NOT hold up — re-measured on the day, immediately before and after, the
count was unchanged: one high either side, nanoid GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8,
reached only through vitest -> vite -> postcss and therefore dev-only.
So the number that gates anything is the one CI actually runs, `npm audit
--prefix functions --omit=dev --audit-level=high`, and that reports 0 on
the runtime tree — the same 0 the top of this block claims, still true
after the bump. The stale prediction is recorded rather than deleted
because the lesson is the shape of the mistake: an advisory count measured
once and written into prose is a figure with no gate behind it, and the
ecosystem moves underneath it. Re-measure before believing this paragraph.
Note also that ci.yml's audit job is `continue-on-error: true` on purpose
— advisory only, so an advisory published overnight cannot block an
emergency rules deploy. The weekly security-audit workflow is the one that
fails loudly. Neither of them was what refused this bump; a comment was.
